question: What are the recommended procedures for inspecting restraint systems in relation to scheduled intervals and component life limits?
answer: Inspect the restraint system in accordance with the time intervals set forth in Chapter 5, Inspection Time Limits. In addition to these scheduled inspections, the restraint assemblies have life limits. Refer to Chapter 5, Component Time Limits.

title: SEAT BELTS/RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the steps involved in removing and installing the pilot's and copilot's seat belt/restraint assemblies in the aircraft?
answer: NOTE:  The seat belt/restraint assembly removal/installation is typical for restraints in all locations.Pilot's and Copilot's Seat Belt/Restraint Removal . (1) Remove the access cover on the overhead console to get access to the restraint inertia reel assemblies. (2) Remove the nuts, bolts, and washers that attach the inertia reel assemblies to the bracket assembly. (3) Remove the nuts, washers, bolts, and spacers that attach the restraint assemblies to the seats.Pilot's and Copilot's Seat Belt/Restraint Installation . (1) Attach the restraint inertia reel assemblies to the bracket assembly above the overhead console with the bolts, washers, and nuts. (2)  Install the access cover on the overhead console. (3) Attach the restraint assemblies to the seats with the bolts, washers, spacers, and nuts. (4)  Do a check of the system for correct installation and operation.Bench Seat Restraint Removal . (1) Remove the bolt and the washer that attach the seat restraint inertia reel to the aft cabin structure. (2)  Remove the bolts, washers, and spacers that attach the restraint inertia reels to the seat frame.Bench Seat Restraint Installation . (1) Attach the restraint inertia reels to the seat frame with the spacers, washers, and bolts. (2)  Attach the restraint inertia reels to the aft cabin structure with the washers and the bolts.

title: SEAT BELTS/RESTRAINTS - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What are the procedures and safety precautions to follow when removing and installing restraint system components in an aircraft equipped with inertia style reels and AMSAFE inflatable restraints?
answer: The airplane has inertia style reels which let the user lean forward, but will lock in position with sudden movement. The seat belts retract and stow in position when not in use. This maintenance practices section covers removal and installation for restraints used in both the front and rear positions.The restraint system components are non-repairable field items. If any component in the restraint system is not operating correctly, the system must be replaced. WARNING: If the airplane has AMSAFE inflatable restraints, do not do maintenance on the seat belts until you look at and obey all applicable precautions and instructions supplied in AMSAFE publications and this Maintenance Manual.  If you do not obey and follow these instructions and safety precautions, damage to equipment and harm to personnel can occur.If your airplane has the AMSAFE inflatable restraint system, do not do maintenance on the seats or the seat restraint system unless you first obey all applicable precautions and instructions in the E508804 Supplemental Amsafe Maintenance Manual and this Maintenance Manual. Refer to Inflatable Restraint System - Maintenance Practices.
